quote: feel every added detail as a burden, even a single extra roll of the dice
content: The essay is making a claim about probability, and Popper’s trade-off is that claim, stated approvingly. Added content lowers probability; that is why a detailed theory must be paid for with evidence, and the whole of the sequence’s treatment of Occam’s Razor is the other half of the ledger. Nothing here recommends preferring the disjunction: it recommends noticing that you have spent probability, so that you notice when you have spent it on details that bought you nothing, which is what the futurist adding a plausible-sounding clause has done. Newton’s laws are indeed less probable a priori than "bodies move somehow," and were bought with two centuries of observation.

quote: where the absurdity is the log probability, so you can add it
content: The qualitative moral survives the loss of independence, because the inequality does. P(A&B) ≤ min(P(A), P(B)) is a theorem with no independence assumption, so every added conjunct can only lower the probability, which is the entire content of "feel every added detail as a burden." Additivity in log-space is the special case, flagged in the essay by "roughly," and correlation between conjuncts can only make the joint more probable than the sum of absurdities implies, never less — so the error, where it occurs, runs against the essay’s conclusion and the conclusion holds anyway. Support theory explains why unpacking inflates judged probability; it does not make the unpacked conjunction more probable.
